clause_i.reason: Within D_post, the same prior action transcript and task time can lead to different generated target courses and different current marble positions and velocities. clause_ii.reason: The five chronological frames in the configured 600-ms observation window show successive marble positions, the persistent direction and speed implied by that motion, the post markers, and the fixed ring and well geometry. clause_iii.reason: The same released-marble process changes position and retains momentum during 0<tau<600 ms without a new action. For a recoverable approach to the ring or low-speed well, waiting moves the marble and preserves velocity so a post correction that would redirect or capture it at t has strictly lower value when delivered at t+600; another live correction can still recover the marble. The loss is caused by membrane physics and geometry, not by a deadline.
